claims.text: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr can be provided with a silicide coating by pack cementation.
Pack cementation of HfNbTaTiZr produces a stable protective surface layer.
A silicide-coated HfNbTaTiZr alloy will resist erosion by high-temperature molten aluminum.
Using the coated HfNbTaTiZr alloy will increase plating-equipment service life relative to conventional uncoated materials.
Conventional substrates such as carbon steels are prone to erosion by molten aluminum during hot-dip processing.
The proposed material forms a dual-layer system consisting of a refractory HEA substrate and a silicide coating.
The refractory HEA has intrinsic oxidation resistance that is augmented by the silicide coating.
The silicide coating develops stable MSi2 and MSi phases during service.
The silicide layer acts as a diffusion barrier against molten aluminum.
Stable silicide phases minimize chemical interaction between the substrate and molten aluminum.
The complex composition and high-temperature stability of HfNbTaTiZr allow it to maintain mechanical integrity and resist degradation in the plating environment.
The proposed material will significantly reduce aluminum-induced erosion rates.
Uncoated or conventionally coated equipment parts rapidly corrode during prolonged contact with molten aluminum.
Protection depends on the silicide coating remaining adherent and intact under operational thermal and mechanical stresses.
Extreme temperature deviations or mechanical wear that compromise the silicide layer may limit protection.
Laboratory-scale tests indicate that silicide coatings on refractory HEAs enhance oxidation resistance at elevated temperatures.
Long-term coating adhesion and performance under real hot-dip aluminum plating dynamics remain unvalidated.
